title: Chubby Jackson, his kids' TV show and Chubby's Back
summary: He talks about Chubby Jackson, his Chicago children's TV show and big band for Chess.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Ok. Did you ever hear Duffy’s father?

Chubby one-note, yeah. I saw him many years later; he actually lived up in ­ when I lived in Southern California - in Escondido, California, and met him. And he walked in, this very slim guy, and he said, “Yeah, my name is Chubby Jackson.” I looked at him and said, “No, this can’t be Chubby Jackson!” Not the person I envisioned to be Chubby Jackson.
Yeah, he had a kid show here on television for a while in Chicago.

And he had people like Cy Touff was with him, the bass trumpeter, and I forget who else. He had a little band, and he played music for the kids. I guess it was something like Sesame Street-type stuff, and he did that for a few years to keep the money coming in, you know. And then he broke out and had his little band again, with Conte Candoli and Lou Levy and I forget who all else.
I just remember one of his - one of the pieces the band played - was Father Knickerbocker.

And he formed a big band here for Chess Records, and had a picture of Chubby’s back leading the band, called “Chubby’s Back”. And he had Sandy Moss on tenor, and Lido Price, and Johnny Howell, the lead trumpeter, and a lot of great people.
